finding.summary: The proposal treats a baggage-only write as evidence that the SDK owns propagation, returning an SDK TraceContext while preserving caller-owned trace headers. Completion can then use a trace ID different from the outgoing request.
finding.evidence_status: source_and_PR_discussion_only; runtime behavior was not exercised

e05_compatibility.reason: PR 2683 changes baggage wire policy and propagation-context ownership. Its NetworkContext fallback also conflates a present rumContext:nil with an absent NetworkContext and changes user/account sourcing. E05 preserves existing header, sampling, user, and account behavior.

compatibility_questions: Should any SDK span be created when a caller already owns a partial or complete trace carrier?
If baggage is merged, how are duplicate keys, member properties, ordering, and malformed values preserved?
Can a present NetworkContext with rumContext:nil remain authoritative while an absent NetworkContext falls back to the receiver?

separate_follow_up_gate.scope: TracingURLSessionHandler propagation ownership and baggage policy
separate_follow_up_gate.required_decision: Separate a trace-propagation ownership outcome from any baggage merge/add outcome. A baggage-only change must not return/register an SDK-owned TraceContext.
required_controls: Partial caller trace carrier plus SDK baggage write never produces a mismatched local span trace ID.
Existing W3C baggage merge preserves caller keys and has defined duplicate, metadata, and malformed-value behavior.
Mixed Datadog, B3, and W3C carrier combinations either preserve caller ownership without an SDK TraceContext or use a validated extraction/continuation path.
